Usage: drive cleanup [<session>] [flags]

Remove what closed sessions left once it is merged, and say plainly what stays.

A closed session's merged branch goes with its worktree. One that is not
merged stays, as does one gwt will not remove, such as a checkout with
uncommitted work or a branch an open session is on: it prints why, status
lists it once as a fact, and nobody is asked. What stays is judged again on
the next run, since a pull request can merge after its session closed. gwt
keeps a recovery ref for anything it discards.

Arguments:
  <session>            One closed session of the batch, instead of every closed session of the
                       driver's batches (optional).

Inherited flags:
  -h, --help           Show context-sensitive help.
      --batch=NAME     Act in this batch, as drive prints its name, instead of the driver's current
                       one. It may stand anywhere on the line.
      --driver=NAME    Act in the batch this driver drives now; a chat driver's name is its
                       webhook's. It may stand anywhere on the line.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    refused: nothing was done; next: says what to run instead
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run
  3    tried and did not end as asked; the message says what did happen
  4    the session's login was rejected; next: relaunches it on another account, or says to tell the
       owner
